findings.reason: a worker implementing §5 literally leaves cli.py's flat single-engine publisher writing the composer's own lane.json, so the default-pool document can be overwritten by a one-engine document (or by a submitted refresher job) and the aggregation §5 specifies silently disappears.
findings.text: §5 asserts of its named composer that "No other function writes a lane document", but `imas_ambix/agent/cli.py`'s `lane()` command is a second writer of the same file: it computes `document_path = Path(site.endpoint_document).with_name("lane.json")` and calls `write_lane_document` (cli.py:3840, 3868), and its `--submit` path generates and submits a long-lived refresher job (`generate_lane_refresher_script`), so the one-writer invariant the section rests its "no two files carry the same fields" guarantee on cannot hold as written.

findings.reason: the gate has to name the tree the renderer actually lands in, or the anti-regression check cannot fire against the artifact it exists to protect.
findings.text: §10 moves gpu-watch's renderer into `imas_ambix/agent/gpu_watch/` (line 538) but then says "The done-when's symbol check runs against dotfiles after that commit", while the check itself (line 563) is on "gpu-watch's source" carrying no `serve_grid`/`callers_table`/`serve_ledger_table` and no hard-coded node name. The checked source is therefore the package module, not dotfiles, and a leftover serve-panel symbol or hard-coded node name in the package module passes a dotfiles-only grep.
